$comment: The world's elevation and its water (ARCHITECTURE.md §6.3, docs/WORLD_GENERATION.md, ADR 0049, ADR 0074): one world-scale system, not per biome (owner, 2026-11-10: "the elevation separate from biomes"; mountains come from the elevation). Heights in metres above sea level, distances and wavelengths in metres, slopes in m per m. `inland`, `seaFloor`, `hills` and `bumps` are the base height field: the input the world map samples on its 100 m grid before the uplift layer and the erosion (shared/worldgen/hydrology.json); chunks never read it directly. `rivers` the channels carved from the map's river polylines, `mouths` their deltas and estuaries, `lakes` the lake shores, `spawn` where players start. `defaultBiome` names the biome (shared/worldgen/biomes/*.json) layered on the elevation: its surface bands and fine relief. Prototype content (§6.1). Changing any value changes the terrain a seed generates: regenerate the goldens (`cargo run -p dwell-worldgen --example goldens`) and ship it on a new compatibility line. Run `node shared/worldgen/gen.mjs` after editing; CI fails on stale output.

islands.$comment: The coast broken into islands (ADR 0074 B4, the archipelago's knob): with amplitude > 0 the island's signed coast distance is capped at cap m and offset by a fractal noise of ±amplitude m at wavelength m (octaves), so the coast weaves into bays, straits and islands; the inland rise and the shelf then follow each island's own coast. 0 (the default world's): the one island as before.

tectonics.$comment: Tectonics at realistic scale (systemic terrain T5, ADR 0075): one plate boundary crossing the island and one hotspot chain offshore, added to the base height field before the world map's uplift and erosion. The boundary is a line angle degrees from +x toward +z, offset m from the centre along its normal (the overriding plate on its + side). kind: 0 none, 1 convergent (subduction: a range rangeHeight m high and width m half-wide behind the line, a trench trenchDepth m deep before it, and a volcanic arc), 2 divergent (a rift riftDepth m deep and width m half-wide with raised shoulders; lakes fill its floor), 3 transform (ridges across the line, the two sides offset by shift m). The arc (convergent only): arcCount dormant stratovolcanoes arcDistance m behind the line, arcSpacing m apart, coneHeight m high and coneRadius m wide, each with a crater craterRadius m wide and craterDepth m deep, its cone's erodibility scaled by 1 − coneHardness (0..1; toward the summit, so a tall cone such as a 4800 m Rainier keeps its relief through the world map's erosion, its crater cut again after it). The hotspot chain: hotspotCount islands from (hotspotX, hotspotZ) along hotspotHeading degrees (the plate's motion), hotspotSpacing m apart, the youngest hotspotHeight m over the sea floor, each older one hotspotDecay of the last's height and hotspotWiden broader (eroded). coreDistance: m behind a convergent line where the old core's rock begins (rocks.json tectonic). The arc cones' shape (0.52.40, a Rainier, not a Fuji): ridgeCount radial ridges with glacier-cut valleys between them up to ridgeDepth m deep (deepest just below the summit, none at the foot), their spacing made irregular by ridgeWarp (radians); the summit summitOffset m off the cone's centre toward summitAngle degrees (the foot stays put, so one flank is steeper); a shoulder peak shoulderHeight m high and shoulderRadius m wide shoulderDistance m from the summit toward shoulderAngle; ventCount parasitic cones ventHeight m high and ventRadius m wide ventDistance m from the centre. A crater whose rim stands above iceAbove m (above the sea) holds an ice dome iceDome m over its rim instead of a hollow (no crater lake above it). The snow line: where the climate (vegetation.json, the biome map's temperature with its lapse rate) is below snowBelowC °C, the ground is rocks.json tectonic.snow, except where steeper than snowMaxSlope (rise per run: ridges stay bare rock). All neutral by default (no ridges, no offset, no shoulder or vents, iceAbove 100000, snowBelowC −100). Off in the default world (kind 0, no hotspots): the terrain is unchanged.

rivers.$comment: Channels from the map's river polylines (smoothed `smooth` times, corner cutting). A column's nearest river by its channel's edge: inside the channel the bed lies depth (the map's width curve) below the water at the centre, at least minDepth; beyond it the ground is cut down to a valley rising from bank m over the water (as steeply as the biome's `banks.riverSlope`), out to reach m plus reachPerWidth × the width, where it meets the land; where the land is lower than the water the banks are raised to bank m over it (levees), falling away leveeFall m per m to the land, a broad bank rather than a ridge; none where the river is at sea level (its water is the sea's). Where a river joins another it reaches the other's level joinMargin m plus its own half-width outside the other's channel, and falls to it at most joinSlope m per m upstream of there (a short gorge where it hangs above the other). Meander: the banks are traced through a warp of about ±meander m at meanderWavelength. The LOD widens a river at least lodMinShare of its cell size wide to lodWidth × its cell size, at cells up to lodMaxCell m, so rivers show from afar. Where a river's surface steps down a row, the water falls a row from one pool to the next, the bed under each at its own depth: no lips (BUGS.md #29, Phase 53 G1a; the water surface grid rests the water as drawn). A chute (its steps closer than a row every 2.5 m) has a dry bed a row under its surface and a stream down its middle as wide as its river's flow needs.

mouths.$comment: Where a big river meets the sea (the map marks deltas and estuaries): over its last reach m its channel widens, an estuary's to estuaryWiden × its width and estuaryDeepen × its depth (a funnel), a delta's to deltaWiden × its width, and a delta splits into deltaBranches distributaries at deltaSplit m from the sea, spreading deltaSpread degrees either side, each deltaBranchWidth of the river's width.

lakes.$comment: A lake is flat at its level, inside its cells of the map (traced through a warp of ±shoreNoise m at shoreWavelength); round it the ground stands at least the biome's `banks.lake` m over the water for levee m (falling `banks.lakeSlope` m per m from 2 m out), so the water never stands open beside lower ground.

spawn.$comment: Players spawn on level dry land between minHeight and maxHeight m above sea level, preferring a river within nearRiver m: the map's cells are ranked by their distance from the disc's centre (the land nearest it first), and the first that suits is searched for a level patch.

biomeMap.$comment: The biome map's geography (ADR 0074 B2): a slow climate gradient across the island (0..1 from one side to the other, along a direction from the seed, bent by a noise of climateWavelength m and ±climateNoise), temperature = climate − lapseRate per 1000 m of elevation; wetness easing from 1 at a river or lake to 0 wetReach m away; a biome border dithered by a noise of ditherWavelength m (±dither of the weights), so edges are not lines. Only read where a world has more than one biome. The rain shadow (systemic terrain T1): a prevailing wind blowing from windDirection degrees (face-local, from +x toward +z) carries moisture in from the sea (refilled to 1 over sea) and drops it as rain: baseRain of it per km on flat land, more where the ground rises along the wind (upliftRain per 10 % grade), less where it falls behind high ground (leeDry per 10 % grade); the air dries out over windReach m of full rain, so land behind a ridge gets what is left. The wetness a biome reads is (1 - rainShare) x the river/lake wetness + rainShare x the rainfall: rainShare 0 (the default) is the wetness without rain, so the default world is unchanged; tune it in Chisel. The wind sees the ground low-passed over windSmoothM m (a tent filter; 0: the map's own heights), so a whole range lifts the air and shadows its lee, not each hillside.
